seo.title: What is a punchout catalogue?
seo.description: A punchout catalogue lets a procurement buyer shop your site with their agreed pricing and return with the basket as a requisition.

definition: A punchout catalogue lets a buyer leave their own procurement system, shop on your site with their agreed pricing, and return with the basket as a requisition.
answerBlock: A punchout catalogue lets a buyer leave their own procurement system, shop on your site with their agreed pricing, and return with the basket as a requisition. It is a B2B pattern for customers whose purchasing runs through a procurement platform. The order is then approved inside their system rather than paid on your checkout.

body.heading: How does a punchout session work?
paragraphs: The buyer clicks through from their procurement system, which sends a request identifying the account. Your site opens a session that knows who they are, shows their contracted prices, and, when they finish, sends the basket back to their system rather than taking payment.

The details are unglamorous: session security, catalogue mapping, unit-of-measure agreement and part-number alignment with the customer's own codes. Most of the effort is in that alignment, not in the shopping journey.
It only makes sense with a clean catalogue and reliable account pricing behind it, which is why it is usually the second phase of a B2B project rather than the first.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: For a distributor, punchout is often the condition of doing business with a large customer at all. Being the supplier that is easy to buy from inside their system is a defensible advantage.
It also removes rekeying, which is where order errors come from on both sides.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: Northmark Supply's counter staff stopped retyping orders once the quoting platform was tied into the ERP, which is the same benefit punchout gives the customer's purchasing team.

service.title: Ecommerce development

terms.definition: A payment gateway is the service that takes a card or bank payment from a customer and moves the money to your account.
A product catalogue is the structured record of everything you sell: the products, their variants, their attributes and how they are grouped.
